title: Mushroom Risotto Cakes
subtitle: crispy fried risotto cakes with a golden breadcrumb crust
excerpt: Risotto cakes use leftover or freshly made mushroom risotto shaped into patties, coated in breadcrumbs, and fried until golden. The outside is crunchy; the inside is creamy and rich. They work as a starter or a light main with a simple salad.
sourceNotes: Risotto cakes, sometimes called arancini when made with a filling, are a staple of Italian cucina povera -- using up leftover risotto from the day before.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the risotto a day ahead. Chill well before shaping and frying.

content.text: The risotto must be cold and firm before you shape it. Warm risotto will not hold. Make it ahead and chill for at least 30 minutes.
Fry the mushrooms in butter over high heat until golden. Remove and set aside.
In the same pan, soften the onion in a little oil. Add the garlic, then the rice. Stir for 1 minute.
Add the wine. Stir until absorbed. Add the hot stock a ladleful at a time, stirring constantly and waiting for each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. This takes about 20 minutes.
Stir in the mushrooms, parmesan, and butter. Season. Spread on a tray and cool. Chill for at least 30 minutes.
Shape the cold risotto into 8 patties. Dip each in beaten egg, then breadcrumbs.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Fry the cakes for 3 to 4 minutes each side until deeply golden. Drain on kitchen paper. Serve at once.

items.cause: Risotto was too warm or too loose
items.fix: Chill the risotto for longer. The mixture must be cold and firm.

items.symptom: Breadcrumbs are burning before the inside heats through
items.fix: Lower the heat and cover the pan for 1 minute to heat the interior.

content.text: Risotto cakes are a form of cucina povera -- the Italian tradition of using up every last bit of food. Leftover risotto becomes the base for a dish that is better than the original in terms of texture contrast. The Sicilian arancino is the most famous version, typically stuffed with meat or cheese. Flat pan-fried versions like these are quicker and more forgiving.
